The Mender stands up "As this is a formal address.... I assume proper names are a something to use... Last time I was here.... I was known as The Honorable Judge, Baron Sandigill, Eldest Chinnokin of the Roanoak Colony and Priest of the Twin Vents School, Member of the Mid Atlantic Nation.  Most of that title is meaningless now..." He thinks for a moment "These days... I guess my proper  name now would just be Mender Sandigill of Murry Hill."  He has a pensive look at he takes a moment to look out a window, and pulls out a bag of good berries from her vest and eats one.  After a moment he continues "I have some wisdom... or maybe a warning... to pass on.  I have seen suggestions of divided power.  Last time.... we tried that.  Every decision.... every need.... bogged down in bureaucracy.  Every decision was discussed.... and discussed.... and questioned..... almost to the point that the town couldn't get along.  The divisions... the fractures.... caused by loyalties to one person or another..... meant very little got done.  That was 5 people managing a town of maybe 100.  I lost my life to their indecision.... their inability to work togeather.  The work we did.... is lost to time.  I believe they won after my passing.... as I don't think I could even be here had they failed."  He eats another goodberry.  
He shakes his head and continues "A leader must be able to act... to react.  The more people that are involved in making a decision.... the more time everything takes.... and the more room for corruption to seep in.  If you have 1 leader.... either that person is corrupt or not.  With 100 people making decisions.... all you need are half to be greedy.... self serving... to corrupt your process.  You don't even need that.  5 or 10 people can convince 40 or 50 to corruption.  It's easier to identify 1 corrupt person on a pedestal than it is 5 in a crowd."
He pauses once more collecting his thoughts "We **have** seen good kings in history... single people that have lead their people well. Single people that love and provide for their people.   And when we see the like of *King George III* the people rise up.... fight.  You don't have to depend on dividing the power to save the people.  You have to depend on good people to stand up to a corrupt leader.  And that is easier with a single person wearing the target.  I won't tell you the best way to run your new country... but I will suggest that you look to the fallen republic of Greece.... the fall of the triumvirate in Rome.... if you want to see what splitting the power does."
he takes one more moment to eat another goodberry "I have seen the very souls of the people here.... everyone has the potential to do wrong.... but I would say most of your hearts are i the right place.  I think Roy has some good points.... I think elections are smart.... beyond that.... You might consider a leader and cabinet of experts approach..." he pauses one last time "This is your new world... so I can't tell you what is best.  You have to consider the native tribes that live here... the war on the other side of the ocean.... the immigrants that are here.... and continue to move here.... and decide if you want a better world today.... or wait for many voices to waste time deciding on what first step to take.... So at least consider the boons of a single leader... for I have witnessed that failure of split government first hand."  he says.  Then quietly goes to an edge of the room to sit down."

Finn takes in the points before speaking
"I read about the division of labor in the Roanoke colony. They split the power into three different jobs. An ambassador, mayor, and captain of the guard of sorts. Their biggest failure was in their communication and lack of meetings. A group of 3 that concern themselves only with leading and not with adventuring as well seems like it would dilute that problem. 

As for the ravens or other divine beings. Sure they may be useful guardians and can be personally sought after for help, but I definitely want them to have no part in shaping the future of the world if we can help it. A complete separation of church and state. For those that don't follow the ravens for example, I wouldn't want the country's policies to be something a non believer would have to adhere to. Whomever is elected into power can seek out that guidance on their own time, but I don't want our system of government to rely on a godlike being. They die, squabble, war, and fight each other for power over domains. That's a headache we don't need."
Somewhere pigeon thinks to itself "we have head bands of intellect. Now we just need nose rings of compassion. Then a good leader is guarenteed."

"we will need a way to handle conflicting religions. I'm sure there's a handful that we could all agree don't belong, the ones that live to cut down everything else, but when the communities are mashed together what happens when tension flares?"

The mender stands to address Finn "5.  Orriginally it was three, Mayor, Judge, and General.... but it expanded quickly to 5.  Mayor Copper was to run the day to day, and be a leader of the people... Captian of the guard as you put it Cato.... Who was in charge of defense and protection..... Ambassador Viola.... who was to be the representative of... and to... the local native tribes.... Spymaster Web.... who kept a finger on the pulse of town... and got leaders the info they needed.... and Judge Sandigil.... who upheld and enforced the law no matter the personal costs.  Some stayed back, some went out.... Finn... I was there.... who survived to write the books?  Those histories are not truth of what happened.... Every decision took days... When we needed to keep our word and work together.... Web was panning a wedding and working on zombies.... Cato was running off to battle to be the front line.... Copper was indecisive and needed support.... Viola ignored by the people not of the land.... and I was having to pass judgement on lawbreakers who were family.... which only sewed discord.  People were loyal to one or another of us.... and so the town was fractured.  We thought a counsel... picked by the people... to represent different aspects of governance was the way to go.... But all it did was get many of us killed.  I was informed by another who was there at the end.... most of the counsil stepped down after my death.  In the end.... there was only one that ran that town." and sits back down

"I bring up the ravens not as a believer, but as someone who has interacted with them. You don't need to have faith in them to see that they have power, power over thought and memory." The Speaker replies to Captain Midask, giving occassional glances to Irynx, the priestess of the twins. 
"Seperation of church and state does have its merits, but it poses a major flaw. It weakens the state and allows the church free reign. You will not be able to impose laws, taxes, or other regulations on churches because they will claim that they are seperated. We do not need seperation but integration. We should use all possible ways to help run our nation. If three questions asked from the ravens are enough to determine who is the best leader among us then why not ask."
"I also once again agree with the Mender. Power concentrated in the hands of someone competent is much more effective than power diluted among the many. We live in a dangerous world, one that may never be truly safe, we must be decisive and quick."

"Speaker, Mender, your words and experiences have great merit. However, we have time. Let us not fear monger that we must see quick decisive action at every moment. We're building a nation we hope to never outlive. A small dilution of power allows a system for checks and balances where discourse and greater representation of the ideals is in line with the people. Compromises between 3 would theoretically give dissenters the ability to have their voice considered instead of outright dismissed by an opposing leader. "
A Dwarf wearing naught but a blacksmiths apron walks in and stands at the back.
He crosses his arms and looks surly.

"We are here discussing, but we are still at war Captain Midask. Where is this time you speak of?" The Speaker pauses for effect. "In the future, when this terrible conflict is naught but a sad story, maybe there will be time. Time to spend carefully crafting the perfect system. But this is not yet that future, we cannot be caught debating for too long."
"I still agree with your call for balance and for everyone being brought into the political fold. But for a compromise, we can implement a transitional government. A government where power is focused so that rapidity of actions is observed. A government that will use everything in its power to bring back a semblance of order to this chaos. A government that can control things long enough as to allow us to go into more depth about a better system that will outlive us. "

"We should run our country different from how we run it during wartime. The transitional government I ask for is one that will start the change from a highly militaristic government to one we can hold during times of peace. Washington and our current army should not be bothered with matters of law, they have redcoats to beat."

"With the approval of the people and enough votes, whatever government we put into place would have the power to keep striving for a perfect system. I don't see why we shouldn't try to do the heavy lifting now. 

We have already come so far in the midst of this war. Building a nation at the same time is something every one of us will be the unique experts at in this world.
Let us put in the systems they need to better prepare, but let us not sacrifice systems of oversight for haste of decisions.

Guiding a nation is an insurmountable task to hold the responsibility for alone. With a guided cabinet of experts, two branches for the implementation of law and change, and a small council that leads the nation with arms together, leadership still has the ability to make quick decisions rather than have a full committee for each discourse."
